newsitem.title: USA: Merchandise from movie tie-ins to hit stores soon.
newsitem.headline: Merchandise from movie tie-ins to hit stores soon.

text.p: The world's strongest man, the world's most beautiful lost princess and the world's wiliest alien fighters are coming to stores near you.

Characters from "Hercules," "Anastasia," "Men in Black" and the re-released "Star Wars" trilogy will flood into stores this year, and, aided by heavy television advertising, will likely define what children want come birthdays and holidays.

Hoping to recreate the success of Disney's "Lion King" and extend the 20 year love affair with Lucasfilm Ltd.'s "Star Wars" characters, toy manufactures and major studios have teamed up this year to give children what they think kids need -- heros who take on the bad guys and beautiful ladies who get their man.
In the hero department comes "Hercules," the Walt Disney Co. animated movie that opens in June, about the adventures of the mythical hero.

Mattel Inc. has developed Golden Glow Hercules, a doll with beefy muscles and dressed in ancient Grecian-style armour. He transforms from a mere mortal to a "glowing" hero when held in direct sunlight and his skin gets a "tan" ($17).
Hercules' lady love, Megara, comes in a full-length gown that transforms into a short toga ($17). In a boxed gift set, Hercules and Fashion Secrets Megara sell for $25.

20th Century Fox, in its first foray into animated musical features, will release "Anastasia" in November. The title character is a beautiful orphan, who happens to be the lost princess and youngest child of Russia's last czar.

Fashion dolls based on Anastasia and Dimitri, her romantic interest, will hit stores in October, and sell for $14.99 to $25.99. Fashions for the pair are based on scenes in the movie, as well as "inspired by historical styles of the period," Galoob Toys Inc. says. The accessories will sell for $5.99 to $6.99.

Space aliens bent on interplanetary destruction will meet their match from "Men in Black." Starring Tommy Lee Jones and Will Smith, this child-friendly summer release from Columbia Pictures and Amblin Entertainment has spawned action figures ($5.99 to $6.99) and deluxe action figures with "exploding" body parts ($9.99 to $14.99).
There is also Ultra Alien Terrorist Edgar ($14.99 to $16.99), the ultimate alien foe, who must be stopped from completing his mission -- an intergalactic political assassination.

All "Men in Black" toys are from Galoob, which is also adding to "Aliens" and "Predator" lines with palm-sized vehicles based on the science-fiction movies. The Aliens and Predator Action Fleet vehicles ($9.99 to $11.99) carry action figures, have rotating gun turrets and retractable landing gear.

Another science fiction film, slated for release in November, is "Starship Troopers," from TriStar and based on the book by Robert Heinlein. An army of giant ants launches an attack on Earth and the Starship Troopers travel to the bug planets to save humanity.
Deluxe Bugs and Deluxe Vehicles by Galoob are each sold with two figures, such as Warrior Bug, Hopper Bug, Plasma Bug and Tanker Bug ($9.99 to $11.99).
A remote control Hopper Bug ($24.99 to $29.99) "charges" into action and the Drop Ship ($24.99 to $29.99) fires missiles and "hovers" to allow children to deploy and rescue their troops.

Universal Pictures' "The Lost World: Jurassic Park," director Steven Speilberg's sequal to the original dinosaur adventure, will open May 23 and Hasbro Inc.'s Kenner Division has a line of toys tied to the movie ($5.99 to $49.99).

Toys include Biting Dinos, with electronic roaring sounds ($14.99), Thrasher T-Rex ($29.99), which has a kid-operated biting jaw, and Electronic Bull T-Rex ($39.99), the biggest and most ferocious dinosaur of them all. Electronic Bull T-Rex makes an attack roar, a warning roar and a crunching sound.

"The Lost World" will be anything but lost, Universal says, with a $250 million advertising and promotion budget and additional tie-ins to Burger King, General Mills, Hershey, Kodak and Mercedes Benz products.
The force will be with "Star Wars" enthusiasts, with Hasbro offering new versions of movie-based action figures to coincide with the trilogy's 20th anniversary and re-release.

Basic action figure sets ($4.99 per set and up) are available. Also to be introduced later this year is the Star Wars Collectable Figure Maker, which comes with moulds and air hardening compound to make Luke, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Yoda, droids and various space creatures ($6.99).
Galoob has Death Star Double Takes, part of its line of Micro Machines transforming toys, which is the Death Star on the outside and the planet Tatooine on the inside ($34.99 to $49.99).

Tiger, which specialises in hand-held electronic toys and games, has various "The Lost World" and "Star Wars" products, including talking key chains and "Way Cool Sounds" pens, which roar like dinosaurs, breath heavily like Darth Vader and give out advice like droid 3CPO ($4.99 to $6.99)
You'll find these and other movie tie-in toys at toy and general retailers in a galaxy near you beginning in April and continuing throughout the rest of the year.
